theFixInOneParagraph: Writer (b)'s membership test stops asking whether a work key is a txgio_parcel prop_id and starts asking what the node's OWN keyspace says. `accountKeyedMembershipVerdict` returns one of FOUR NAMED outcomes, so no caller can read one as another: published-parcel-node (the parcel table publishes this key in its own numbering -- kept); reached-by-published-pair (the county's published pair names it to a prop_id THIS county's parcel index publishes -- kept, counted); declared-no-published-identifier (the county publishes a pair over this run's keys and it does not name this key -- KEPT AND DECLARED, not retired, not excluded); hollow-account-keyed (no pair published for this county -- the pre-P-370 verdict, excluded and retired exactly as before). The second arm reads P-351's pair the OTHER way -- account key -> parcel-index prop_id -- by DELEGATING to the builder P-351 wrote (roles swapped) so the two directions cannot disagree about a key and inherit its three refusals. The declaration needs TWO measured facts and both are read off the run: the county publishes a pair over this run's account-shaped keys (the pair object is handed over only when the read returned rows), AND the parcel table does not use this key's shape at all (parcelTableShapeClasses, measured on the keys this run just resolved). The guard is NOT touched: `accountKeyedBlastRadius` / `assertAccountKeyedBlastRadius` keep their exact-set-equality predicate and their throw. Two per-item appends (was `push(...excluded)` / `push(...kept)`) travel with the fix because without them the guard is unreachable at the scale it exists for.

fleetMemoryScratch.text: A GUARD IS NOT A CONTROL UNTIL IT IS PROVEN REACHABLE AT THE POPULATION IT GUARDS. `push(...arr)` is an argument list, not an append: at ~320k items it throws RangeError and the process dies before any guard on the same path runs. 48491's full-county run at the base commit dies with Maximum call stack size exceeded before P-351's refusal is consulted, so the refusal the incident report describes was only reproducible after the appends were made per-item loops. Two per-item loops are now a condition of the guard working at all, and every future full-county run inherits the fix.

TWO NUMBERING SYSTEMS IN ONE COUNTY MAKE SET-EQUALITY GUARDS NECESSARILY PARTIAL. The blast-radius guard refuses only when the excluded set EQUALS a whole served keyspace. The narrower fix -- move back only the keys the published pair reaches -- leaves 37,334 of 319,480 (11.7%) excluded, and 11.7% is invisible to an equality predicate, so the run proceeds to retire 37,334 live accounts. When a class is measured by equality, any arm that moves PART of the class is unguarded by construction; that is why the shipped rule retires nothing rather than retiring less.

A DECLARATION NEEDS A SECOND FACT, AND THE SECOND FACT HAS A MEASURED PRICE. The declaration (this key is named by no published identifier, therefore kept) is only safe if the county's parcel table does not speak the key's numbering; on Hays 25,712 of 56,629 account-shaped keys match rows of another county's extracts because the staged extracts carry no county column. The second fact (parcelTableShapeClasses, measured on the parcel table's own keys this run resolved) is what keeps 45% of Hays' hollow set from silently leaving the retirement population.

COUNTERS ON THE RUN'S JSON ARE WHAT SURVIVE A DROPPED STDOUT. P-371 carded the publish's lost stdout, which is why the guard's per-keyspace line was on no record. The exclusion count and the two new arm counters (reachedByPublishedPair, declaredNoPublishedIdentifier) now ride the run summary, so a run in which the second published identifier did nothing is legible from outside instead of discovered from a refusal.

MOVED-ONLY-THE-REACHED-KEYS-BACK (the first arm built in this lane). It reads as the conservative choice and is a narrower version of the defect: 37,334 keys of a live declared-roll keyspace stay excluded, and set equality cannot see them. Measured, then rejected; do not re-propose it as a smaller change.

EXCLUDING ON AN UNPARSEABLE KEY: an id the prepass never read is KEPT (verdict published-parcel-node for an empty id), because excluding on a key the pass cannot account for is how a pass drops a row it cannot explain. Asserted in the suite.

RE-READING THE PAIR FROM SCRATCH IN THE SECOND DIRECTION: the reverse builder DELEGATES to P-351's forward builder with the roles swapped rather than parsing rows itself, so the three refusals (no prop_id, one extract naming a key twice, two extracts disagreeing) cannot diverge between the two directions. A second implementation would have been a second opinion.
